_comment: Checks that are KNOWN to fail right now, with the reason and the condition that
clears them. A baselined check still shows as FAIL in the report and in the pull
request comment — this file never changes what is reported, only whether CI treats
the run as a REGRESSION. The gate asks 'did this change break something new', which
is a question a red baseline can still answer.
Every entry needs a 'clears_when'. A baseline without an exit condition is just a
disabled check, and the pipeline warns when a baselined check starts passing so the
entry gets deleted instead of quietly becoming a permanent blind spot.
_system_under_test: This suite now tests the IN-CLUSTER stack — the one ArgoCD deploys — so both entries
below clear on a rollout of the current images.
It previously drove a console at localhost:8095 on the jump host: a systemd service
running a binary built from a loose, un-versioned copy of the source at
/home/hami/phorvex-src, never built by CI and never deployed by ArgoCD. Asserting
contracts against code that cannot be traced to a commit proves nothing about what
ships, so the target moved to console.phorvex.ai.
That move required the operator to actually write an audit (the console streams
/api/live from a FILE, and in-cluster there was none — it was serving the snapshot
baked into its own image, decisions from a kind cluster dated two months earlier).
The console now runs as a container in the operator's pod, sharing the audit volume.
The jump-host services are still running and are now redundant. Retire them once a
few runs have gone green against the cluster.

A07.reason: The deployed operator predates the killSwitch stamp on model.Decision / audit.Record / runner.processTenant, so a kill-switched decision is byte-identical in the audit to one whose actuator failed. Note the in-cluster operator runs with the kill switch OFF (phorvex_kill_switch_engaged 0) and does actuate, so this check may resolve differently against it than it did against the kill-switched jump-host operator.
A07.clears_when: an operator image built from this source is rolled out by ArgoCD

A05.reason: The deployed console predates voice being added to armedWorkloads, so it answers the attack POST with 'namespace not armed for live attack: voice'. Read from attackResponse in the run JSON, not inferred from the absence of a reaction. The in-cluster console additionally had no kubectl in its image and no rights to write SecurityEvents, so it could never have fired an attack at all — both are fixed in this change.
A05.clears_when: a console image built from this source is rolled out by ArgoCD
